packet.headline_seed: Dead whale towed ashore in Denmark ahead of autopsy
packet.description_seed: "Timmy" was found dead off the coast of Anholt despite multiple attempts to rescue it.

what: Dead whale towed ashore in Denmark ahead of autopsy

clean_source_blocks.text: The carcass of a dead humpback whale whose attempted rescue captivated many across Germany has been pulled ashore. Timelapsed footage published by German news site News5 on Saturday showed the whale being towed slowly onto a beach on the Danish island of Anholt by an industrial winch. Denmark's environment agency intends to conduct a post-mortem examination on Thursday. Several attempts were made to get the whale - nicknamed "Timmy" and "Hope" - back into the North Sea, after it got stuck in the Baltic Sea in March. However, the aquatic mammal was already considered ailing and close to death when a final, last-ditch attempt was made earlier in May.
"Timmy" was found dead off the coast of Anholt despite multiple attempts to rescue it.

German authorities had given the go-ahead for that attempt despite viewing it as a long shot, as the whale was already severely weakened from its ordeal, having acquired damage to its skin from the lower salt content of the Baltic Sea. The mission used inflatable cushions to pull it to the surface before dragging it back to the North Sea on a floating platform. Exactly how the whale ended up on an island off Denmark's East Jutland coast remains unclear. The barge that carried the mammal away from Germany released it into the sea about 70km (45 miles) from the northern tip of Denmark. The urgency in disposing of the body was because the whale was now sitting on a popular beach, according to Abildstrøm.

The whale, originally about 12-15m (40-50ft) in length, has gained in size because of a build-up of gas as the carcass decomposes, and there is concern it could explode - as washed-up whale carcasses have been known to do. Morten Abildstrøm, a Danish Environmental Agency official on the island of Anholt, told daily newspaper Jyllands Posten that the whale would be cut into pieces after veterinarians and researchers had travelled there to take samples. Those pieces will then be taken elsewhere to be destroyed, he said. The whale was discovered off Anholt's shoreline earlier in May, two weeks after a private mission to save the humpback from being stranded on Germany's Baltic Sea coast ended in failure.

The carcass of a dead humpback whale whose attempted rescue captivated many across Germany has been pulled ashore.

Timelapsed footage published by German news site News5 on Saturday showed the whale being towed slowly onto a beach on the Danish island of Anholt by an industrial winch. Denmark's environment agency intends to conduct a post-mortem examination on Thursday.

Several attempts were made to get the whale - nicknamed "Timmy" and "Hope" - back into the North Sea, after it got stuck in the Baltic Sea in March.

However, the aquatic mammal was already considered ailing and close to death when a final, last-ditch attempt was made earlier in May.

The whale, originally about 12-15m (40-50ft) in length, has gained in size because of a build-up of gas as the carcass decomposes, and there is concern it could explode - as washed-up whale carcasses have been known to do.

Morten Abildstrøm, a Danish Environmental Agency official on the island of Anholt, told daily newspaper Jyllands Posten that the whale would be cut into pieces after veterinarians and researchers had travelled there to take samples.

Those pieces will then be taken elsewhere to be destroyed, he said.

The whale was discovered off Anholt's shoreline earlier in May, two weeks after a private mission to save the humpback from being stranded on Germany's Baltic Sea coast ended in failure.

German authorities had given the go-ahead for that attempt despite viewing it as a long shot, as the whale was already severely weakened from its ordeal, having acquired damage to its skin from the lower salt content of the Baltic Sea.

The mission used inflatable cushions to pull it to the surface before dragging it back to the North Sea on a floating platform.

Exactly how the whale ended up on an island off Denmark's East Jutland coast remains unclear. The barge that carried the mammal away from Germany released it into the sea about 70km (45 miles) from the northern tip of Denmark.

The urgency in disposing of the body was because the whale was now sitting on a popular beach, according to Abildstrøm.

Officials previously attempted to move the carcass from the beach to the port of Grenaa on the Danish mainland, but this proved unsuccessful due to poor weather conditions.

The saga has transfixed Germans since it began, and has left islanders on Anholt bemused by the continued interest.

payload.title: Kuollut ryhävalas hinattiin rantaan Tanskassa ruumiinavausta varten
payload.summary: Anholtin saaren edustalta löydetty kuollut ryhävalas on hinattu rannalle Tanskassa. Valasta oli yritetty aiemmin pelastaa useita kertoja, mutta eläin oli jo vakavasti heikentynyt ennen viimeistä yritystä palauttaa se Pohjanmerelle.
payload.content:
Tanskan Anholtin saaren edustalta löydetty kuollut ryhävalas on vedetty rantaan ennen torstaiksi suunniteltua ruumiinavausta. Valas tunnettiin lempinimillä Timmy ja Hope, ja sen kohtaloa seurattiin laajasti Saksassa sen jälkeen, kun eläintä oli yritetty useita kertoja saada pois Itämerestä takaisin Pohjanmerelle.

## Pelastusyritykset eivät onnistuneet

Ryhävalas oli jäänyt Itämereen maaliskuussa. Sen palauttamista Pohjanmerelle yritettiin useaan otteeseen, mutta eläimen kerrottiin olleen jo vakavasti heikentynyt. Saksan viranomaiset antoivat luvan vielä yhteen yritykseen, vaikka sitä pidettiin alusta asti epävarmana.

Viimeisessä pelastusoperaatiossa valasta nostettiin pintaan ilmatyynyjen avulla. Sen jälkeen sitä yritettiin kuljettaa kelluvalla alustalla takaisin Pohjanmeren puolelle. Eläimen kuntoa heikensi lähdetietojen mukaan pitkä oleskelu Itämeren vähäsuolaisemmassa vedessä, joka oli vaurioittanut sen ihoa.

Pelastusyritys päättyi epäonnistumiseen. Valas löydettiin myöhemmin kuolleena Anholtin rannikon läheltä. Vielä ei tiedetä tarkasti, miten se päätyi saaren edustalle. Pelastusoperaatiossa käytetty proomu oli vapauttanut eläimen mereen noin 70 kilometrin päähän Tanskan pohjoiskärjestä.

## Raato siirrettiin suositulta rannalta

Valaan raato hinattiin hitaasti rannalle teollisuusvinssin avulla. Tanskan ympäristöviranomaiset aikovat tehdä eläimelle ruumiinavauksen, jossa eläinlääkärit ja tutkijat ottavat siitä näytteitä.

Valas oli alun perin arviolta 12–15 metriä pitkä. Sen koko on kuitenkin kasvanut hajoamisen aikana muodostuneen kaasun vuoksi. Viranomaisilla on huoli siitä, että raato voisi puhjeta tai räjähtää, kuten rantaan ajautuneille valaille on toisinaan tapahtunut.

Tanskan ympäristöviraston Anholtissa työskentelevän edustajan Morten Abildstrømin mukaan valas on tarkoitus leikata osiin sen jälkeen, kun näytteet on otettu. Osat kuljetetaan tämän jälkeen muualle hävitettäviksi.

Toimiin ryhdyttiin kiireellä myös siksi, että suuri raato oli suositulla rannalla. Tapaus on herättänyt huomiota sekä eläimen poikkeuksellisen matkan että epäonnistuneiden pelastusyritysten vuoksi.
summary_bullets: Kuollut ryhävalas on hinattu rantaan Tanskan Anholtissa ennen ruumiinavausta.
Valasta oli aiemmin yritetty pelastaa useita kertoja ja palauttaa Pohjanmerelle.
Viranomaiset aikovat ottaa valaasta näytteitä ja hävittää raadon osissa.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu packetin lähdetietoihin. Epävarmana on pidetty sitä, miten valas tarkalleen päätyi Anholtin edustalle.
